title: The Yearbook of the band room
premise: Edmund Hartwell just wants to survive senior year unnoticed at Hollow Creek High, a school built on the ruins of a 1950s reform school the board quietly demolished. But when the ghost of a student who died there begins leaving notes in ink that shouldn't exist — addressed to Edmund by name, though they never told anyone their name — Edmund is dragged into uncovering what really happened, and why the school board sealed the records. As the notes grow more desperate and other students start remembering things that never happened to them, Edmund realizes the ghost isn't haunting the school; she's asking for help before prom night, the anniversary of her death. Edmund must choose between staying invisible and exposing the board's cover-up, ending with the truth read aloud at prom as the gym doors finally open onto the old building's foundations — and the ghost, named at last, lets go.
about_author: Petra Sandoval is a former high school archivist who spent three years cataloguing a district's sealed records before turning them into fiction. She writes YA horror about institutions, memory, and the kids who refuse to look away.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Three weeks into Hollow Creek High, Edmund has perfected invisibility: headphones, hall passes, no eye contact. A tour of the school's odd architecture — a hallway that ends in painted-over brick — establishes the setting's wrongness. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness, the relief of being unseen.

chapters.title: The First Note
chapters.summary: Edmund finds a folded page inside their locker: 'You're new. You still can. — R.' The ink is dark violet and smears like it's wet, hours later. Edmund assumes a prank but keeps the note. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: unease curdling into a strange, unwelcome feeling of being known.

chapters.title: Ink That Shouldn't Be
chapters.summary: Edmund tests the note: water, bleach, sunlight — nothing fades it. Chemistry partner Priya notices Edmund's obsession and offers to help analyze it; the pigment matches nothing in any database. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forming, curiosity overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: What the Seniors Whisper
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She collects the school's folklore: the ghost of 'Ruthie,' a girl from the reform school era, said to walk the third-floor corridor before disasters. Priya doesn't believe it — until she remembers a fire drill from freshman year she was never part of. Emotional beat: rational skepticism cracking.

chapters.title: Second Period, 1958
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. During a history lecture on the town's founding, Edmund experiences a full sensory flashback — chalk dust, a bell, a girl's voice counting — that isn't theirs. The notes continue, now referencing things Edmund said aloud only in their own head. Emotional beat: terror of losing ownership of one's own mind.

chapters.title: The Board's Quiet Year
chapters.summary: Priya and Edmund visit the public library and find a gap: the school district's minutes skip most of 1958–59, and the reform school's records were 'transferred' to a facility that closed decades ago. POV alternating. Emotional beat: first proof this is a cover-up, not just a haunting.

chapters.title: Ruthie Writes Back
chapters.summary: Edmund answers the note directly and leaves it in the locker overnight. By morning the reply covers three pages: Ruthie Vann, fifteen, died in the old auditorium the night of the spring dance, 1959. She needs someone above ground to open what was buried below. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger, and the weight of being chosen.

chapters.title: Vice Principal Marsh
chapters.summary: The administration notices Edmund's library requests. Vice Principal Marsh — third generation of a family that's always been on the board — offers Edmund a college recommendation letter in exchange for dropping 'the archive hobby.' POV Edmund. Emotional beat: the machinery of institutional power smiling politely.

chapters.title: Shared Memories
chapters.summary: Other students begin experiencing Ruthie's memories: a sophomore recites a pledge he never took; the swim team refuses to enter the pool after seeing tiles that aren't there. Priya documents it all. POV Priya. Emotional beat: dread spreading — the past is leaking, and it's accelerating.

chapters.title: The Foundation Map
chapters.summary: Using blueprints from the county office, Edmund and Priya map the old reform school beneath the current building: dormitories under the gym, an auditorium under the cafeteria, and a sealed stairwell behind the painted brick. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: grim excitement — the geography of the secret made visible.

chapters.title: Down the Stairwell
chapters.summary: After hours, they breach the stairwell. Below: flooded corridors, a rusted door marked RECORDS, and walls scratched with names. Ruthie's presence is strongest here — cold, urgent, almost communicative through touch. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: awe and violation; they are trespassing in a grave.

chapters.title: What Marsh Knows
chapters.summary: Priya tails Marsh and discovers he meets monthly with the last surviving board member from 1959, now ninety-one. She photographs a check stub: hush payments, ongoing, sixty-five years long. POV Priya. Emotional beat: righteous anger hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Price of Looking
chapters.summary: Edmund's grades slip, their scholarship interview goes strangely, and their mother gets a call about 'concerns.' The school squeezes gently, then less gently. Edmund nearly quits. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: the cost of survival versus the cost of silence — the theme made personal.

chapters.title: Ruthie's Last Week
chapters.summary: Through deepening shared memory, Edmund lives fragments of Ruthie's final days: a rebellion in the dorms, a punishment, a promise that 'they'll all know at the dance.' Her death wasn't an accident — she was locked in during the fire. POV Edmund/Ruthie braided. Emotional beat: intimacy across time; Edmund stops being an investigator and becomes a witness.

chapters.title: Prom Committee Politics
chapters.summary: Marsh announces this year's prom will be held in the gym directly above the old dormitories — the first time in decades. Priya realizes the anniversary date aligns exactly. The board wants something contained, or completed. POV Priya. Emotional beat: ticking clock engaged.

chapters.title: The Leaked Page
chapters.summary: Edmund leaks one scanned record page to the school paper; the editor kills the story within hours after a call from the district. Even allies are compromised. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: despair — every official channel is bought or frightened.

chapters.title: Ninety-One Years Old
chapters.summary: Priya and Edmund visit the surviving board member, expecting denial. Instead, the dying man confesses everything and hands over the original incident report he kept out of guilt: forty-one boys unaccounted for, one girl dead, all erased. POV Priya. Emotional beat: the terrible relief of confirmation.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Marsh suspends Edmund and confiscates their materials; the notes stop coming, and Edmund feels Ruthie's absence like a severed limb. Realizing the board plans to seal the lower level permanently after prom — with evidence and maybe people inside — they have one night left. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: cornered, committed.

chapters.title: Prom Night
chapters.summary: Suspended students can't attend — so Edmund walks in anyway, report in hand, Priya livestreaming from the parking lot. Mid-dance, the lights fail, the floor goes cold, and every student simultaneously turns toward the painted brick wall. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Read It Aloud
chapters.summary: Edmund takes the microphone and reads the incident report — the names, the fire, the cover-up — while Ruthie manifests not as horror but as a girl in a dance dress, visible to everyone. Parents filming, board members fleeing, Marsh confessing on camera. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: catharsis; witness as weapon.

chapters.title: The Doors Open
chapters.summary: With the truth spoken publicly, the sealed foundations open — figuratively and literally, as crews find the records room intact by morning. Ruthie, named in the paper's headline, appears to Edmund once more: not a plea, just a goodbye. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: release, mourning, gratitude.

chapters.title: The Yearbook of the Band Room
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the school installs a memorial where the auditorium stood; the yearbook dedicates its final page to the forty-two. Edmund, no longer hiding, signs their full name in the band room's legacy book — the same book Ruthie signed in 1959, discovered on the last page. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: identity claimed; survival that cost something, and was worth it.
